title: Actinomycin D synergizes with Doxorubicin in triple-negative breast cancer by inducing P53-dependent cell apoptosis.
authors: Yang, Hong; Li, Sha; Li, Wan; Yang, Yihui; Zhang, Yizhi; Zhang, Sen; Hao, Yue; Cao, Wanxin; Xu, Fang; Wang, Hongquan; Du, Guanhua; Wang, Jinhua
one_liner_zh: 该文研究放线菌素D与阿霉素在三阴性乳腺癌中的协同抗肿瘤作用及P53凋亡机制，核心为药物协同与细胞凋亡，无蛋白质-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: OBJECTIVES: There are three major subtypes of breast cancer, ER+, HER2+ and triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), namely ER-, PR-, HER2-. TNBC is the most aggressive breast cancer with poor prognosis and no target drug up to now. Actinomycin D (ActD) is a bioactive metabolite of marine bacteria that has been reported to have antitumor activity. The aim of study is to investigate whether ActD has a synergetic effect on TNBC with Doxorubicin (Dox), the major chemotherapeutic drug for TNBC, and explore the underlying mechanism. METHODS: TNBC cell lines HCC1937, MDA-MB-436 and nude mice were used in the study. Drug synergy determination, LDH assay, MMP assay, Hoechst 33342 staining, Flow cytometry, Flexible docking and CESTA assay were carried out. The expression of proteins associated with apoptosis was checked by Western blot and siRNA experiments were performed to investigate the role of P53 and PUMA induced by drugs. RESULTS: There was much higher apoptosis rate of cells in the ActD + Dox group than that in ActD group or Dox group. Expression of MDM2 and BCL-2 was reduced while expression of P53, PUMA and BAX were increased in the groups treated with ActD + Dox or Dox compared to the control group. Furthermore, P53 siRNA or PUMA siRNA tremendously abrogated the cell apoptosis in the groups treated by ActD, Dox and ActD + Dox. Flexible docking and CESTA showed that ActD can bind MDM2. CONCLUSIONS: ActD had a synergetic effect on TNBC with Dox via P53-dependent apoptosis and it may be a new choice for treatment of TNBC.
abstract_zh: 目的：乳腺癌主要有三种亚型，即ER+、HER2+和三阴性乳腺癌（TNBC），后者为ER-、PR-、HER2-。TNBC是最具侵袭性的乳腺癌，预后差，且至今无靶向药物。放线菌素D（ActD）是海洋细菌的一种生物活性代谢物，已有报道其具有抗肿瘤活性。本研究旨在探讨ActD是否与多柔比星（Dox）（TNBC的主要化疗药物）对TNBC具有协同作用，并探索其潜在机制。方法：研究使用TNBC细胞系HCC1937、MDA-MB-436和裸鼠。进行了药物协同性测定、LDH检测、MMP检测、Hoechst 33342染色、流式细胞术、柔性对接和CESTA检测。通过Western blot检查与凋亡相关蛋白的表达，并进行siRNA实验以研究药物诱导的P53和PUMA的作用。结果：ActD + Dox组的细胞凋亡率显著高于ActD组或Dox组。与对照组相比，ActD + Dox或Dox处理组中MDM2和BCL-2的表达降低，而P53、PUMA和BAX的表达升高。此外，P53 siRNA或PUMA siRNA极大地消除了ActD、Dox和ActD + Dox处理组中的细胞凋亡。柔性对接和CESTA显示ActD可与MDM2结合。结论：ActD通过P53依赖性凋亡与Dox对TNBC具有协同作用，可能成为治疗TNBC的新选择。
